items.title: GTA 6's Burger Shot Restaurant Is Expanding Across Florida With Real Meals Inspired by the Game
items.excerpt: GTA 6's fast-food hamburger chain, Burger Shot, is expanding with new locations across Florida starting this weekend thanks to a collaboration with Skinny Louie.
items.content_text: GTA 6's fast-food hamburger chain, Burger Shot, is expanding with new locations across Florida starting this weekend thanks to a collaboration with Skinny Louie. Last month, Burger Shot became available at the Kaseya Center , allowing fans to try the real version of the in-game restaurant during Miami Heat games, courtesy of a partnership with a fast-food joint known as Skinny Louie. The chain is now expanding this activation through its standalone stores across Florida. From November 13 to December 31, stores will feature Burger Shot signage, uniforms, and, of course, a menu themed after items in the game. You can take a look at the menu and some images of the food below. Skinny Louie's Burger Shot Menu THE BLEEDER — TRIPLE Three 100% Black Angus smash patties with yellow American cheese, crispy bacon, pickles, BBQ sauce, and ketchup. BURGER SHOT — SINGLE One 100% Black Angus smash patty with yellow American cheese, shredded lettuce, diced raw onions, and Burger Shot sauce. BURGER SHOT — DOUBLE Two 100% Black Angus smash patties with yellow American cheese, shredded lettuce, diced raw onions, and Burger Shot sauce. CARAMEL MILKSHAKE All of this just goes to show how big GTA 6 has gotten. There aren't many video game franchises that could completely command and rebrand a chain of restaurants, but GTA 6 certainly has that power. The game is already the most pre-ordered title in the history of Xbox and PlayStation's digital stores, and analysts estimate that the game has generated $1 billion in revenue ahead of launch. GTA 6 will officially release next week on November 19 and players can start pre-loading right now . Rockstar has also been trickling out small clips of in-game footage , giving players a taste of what's to come when they load in to Vice City next week.

items.title: The He Who Fights With Monsters Hardcover Books Are on Sale Before Black Friday
items.content_text: Amazon has kicked off its latest '3 for 2' sale on books ahead of Black Friday and there are some terrific new releases in there for LitRPG fans. If you haven't already scooped up the Dungeon Crawler Carl books , for example, now is a great time to do so for cheap. And if you're a fan of Travis Deverell's (AKA Shirtaloon) He Who Fights With Monsters series, you can also grab the first two hardcovers at a discount. The first He Who Fights With Monsters hardcover was released earlier this year and the third book will be arriving next week. This series is my overall favorite LitRPG and a great read if you love Dungeon Crawler Carl . He Who Fights With Monsters is fairly well-known in the LitRPG community already. There have been a total of 13 books released so far and they are all terrific. Similar to Dungeon Crawler Carl, there's a lot of humor and pop-culture references sprinkled throughout a relatively fast-paced story. It definitely leans more fantasy than sci-fi, so expect a lot more magic and a less actual science. The story follows Jason Asano as he wakes up inside a hedge maze in a magical world with new powers and absolutely no hair on his body. His determined and off-balance attitude to his strange new predicament helps him to survive the likes of cannibals, monsters, and even personal relationships with ease. All-in-all, a fantastic book with a morally conflicted main character that you can’t help but love the whole way through. His dark and mysterious powers only make the story all the more interesting. Also check out the Dungeon Crawler Carl books in the sale Seeing as there are only two He Who Fights With Monsters books included in the sale, you will have to purchase one more eligible book to actually get the discount. I'd recommend checking out the Dungeon Crawler Carl hardcovers and the graphic novels, both of which are also buy 2, get 1 free. The first graphic novel is an easy recommendation if you already own these books, I gave it an 8 out of 10 in my review .

items.title: Wolfenstein 3 Confirmed to Be in Development at MachineGames
items.excerpt: As part of the Xbox's 25th anniversary celebration at Xbox Fanfest in Seattle today, developer MachineGames confirmed what had long been rumored: that Wolfenstein 3 is in development.
items.content_text: As part of the Xbox's 25th anniversary celebration at Xbox Fanfest in Seattle today, developer MachineGames confirmed what had long been rumored : that Wolfenstein 3 is in development. MachineGames will once again be developing it. Wolfenstein 2: The New Colossus was released to rave reviews in 2017, but MachineGames then put the series on hold to develop 2024's absolutely stellar Indiana Jones and the Great Circle. But now, Wolfenstein is back on the front burner at the Swedish studio. "Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at Machine Games," Xbox CEO Asha Sharma confirmed on X. "One of gaming’s most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more." Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at @MachineGames. One of gaming's most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more. https://t.co/YyX8LrbTvh — ASHA (@asha_shar) November 12, 2026 MachineGames added on to Sharma's post, which shows a page of the Wolfenstein 3 script, saying simply , "His reputation precedes him," referring to the action described on the script page. "Wolfenstein 3 is in production." The developers also confirmed that actors Brian Bloom (as B.J. Blazkowicz) and Debra Wilson (as Grace Walker) will return via a photo of the pair in the developer's motion-capture studio. Wolfenstein 3 shouldn't come as much of a surprise. Last year, in an interview with Noclip , MachineGames studio head Jerk Gustafsson said the team had "always seen [BJ's story] as a trilogy," adding: "That journey for BJ, even during those first weeks at [id Software], when we mapped out New Order — we still had the plan for at least [BJ], what would happen in the second one and what would happen in the third one. "I think that's important to say, because⁠ — at least, I hope ⁠— we're not done with Wolfenstein yet. We have a story to tell." That's not all that Wolfenstein fans have to look forward to, as the pioneering first-person shooter series is also being developed into a TV series at Amazon. Xbox's official 25th anniversary is this Sunday, November 15.

items.title: A PlayStation 5 Compatible SSD With Heatsink Dropped to Possibly the Lowest Price We'll See for Black Friday
items.excerpt: Grand Theft Auto 6 alone will eat up over 200GB of your total storage.
items.content_text: If you're an avid PS5 gamer, sooner or later you're going to need more storage. Grand Theft Auto 6, which comes out this month, will take up over 200GB of space alone . That's nearly 25% of your stock 1TB storage space, since a 1TB PS5 drive really equates to less than 850GB of usable storage. Unfortunately, PlayStation storage deals are practically non-existent in 2026... but that changes today. Ahead of Black Friday, Walmart just dropped the price of the Verbatim Vi7000 1TB PlayStation 5 compatible solid state drive (SSD) to just $129 with free shipping. This is the lowest price I've seen for a high-speed 1TB SSD in months. If you want even more storage, the 2TB model is also on sale for $199 . Both models even include a built-in heatsink. Never say never, but I think we'll be hard pressed to find a better price than this during Black Friday proper. Black Friday Deal: PS5-Compatible 1TB SSD for $129, 2TB for $199 The Verbatim Vi7000 is Playstation 5 compatible. That means it fulfills all of Sony's requirements. It boasts sequential speeds of 7000MB/s read and 6500MB/s write, which easily surpasses the minimum recommended speed of 5,500MB/s. The SSD uses the PCI-Express Gen4x4 interface which slots neatly into the PS5's drive bay. It also has a preinstalled heatsink that will do a fine job of keeping your SSD cool. The Vi7000 is also a great option as a boot drive for your gaming PC. Surprisingly, this RAM boasts actual DRAM cache. Pretty much every other "budget" SSD at this price point is DRAM-less and relies on HMB, or system memory, as a less expensive alternative. The advantage of having a DRAM cache is faster random read/write performance and faster sustained transfer speeds. It doesn't make much of a difference in a PS5 console but PC users might notice it. items.title: Skydance Owning Both Warner Bros. and Paramount Could Open the Door to a Future of Crossover Slop
items.excerpt: Skydance owning the IP of both Warner Bros. and Paramount opens the door to them possibly doing crossover films one day, a future where $300 million glorified fan fic films could be the next big thing.
items.content_text: What the future holds for DC Studios in a post-James Gunn and Peter Safran world is anyone’s guess at the moment. Perhaps we’ll know more once incoming DC Studios President and Chief Creative Officer Jeremy Latcham assumes command December 1, but I assume there may not be any new film or TV slates officially announced until after the New Year. The biggest question, obviously, is whether the new Skydance-operated regime will reboot Gunn’s DCU , with some reports claiming that might be the case . Skydance is $87 billion in debt and looking to cut costs and maximize profits across the board. Post-merger , Skydance now has all of the Paramount intellectual property at their disposal to exploit as well as the entire Warner Bros. library. So how might such a debt-riddled corporation start producing films that seem like safer commercial bets than, say, a Clayface movie (which was a modest success for DC Studios)? They will obviously lean on their most recognizable, bestselling brands ( hi, Batman! ), but Skydance now owning the IP of both studios opens the door to them possibly doing crossover films one day. That was what many fans thought might happen with Disney and Fox properties after those studios merged , but audiences are only getting their first real taste of that crossover potential with Avengers: Doomsday . That acquisition was completed seven years ago, and I can’t see Skydance wanting to wait that long to jumpstart audience interest in all the new toys they have to play with. Mind you, I’m not advocating for crossover films between Warner Bros. and Paramount IP, but it does seem like something someone at Skydance has to at least consider. A live-action Batman meets the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles movie might sound ridiculous, but those two properties have already done animated film and comic book crossovers , so maybe it’s not as crazy as it sounds. Of course, Paramount has yet to even make a proper Transformers/G.I. Joe crossover movie and they’ve had those properties in-house for ages. There would certainly be a lot of legal entanglements still involved in any Warners/Paramount crossover project despite Skydance owning both studios – producers’ existing deals, credits, etc. – but when you owe $87 billion, maybe kicking around huge event movie ideas like a franchise crossover might not be too crazy to consider. Granted, such crossovers would open the door to Hollywood essentially making fan fic films, but they’re high-concept and marketable to mass audiences. A studio exec could simply type a prompt into AI and have it spit out a list of potential crossover movies, which I feel certain someone at Skydance must have already done. Are we looking at a future where, say, the Justice League teams with the Autobots to stop Lex Luthor and the Decepticons? Where the Terminator is sent into the Matrix or the Green Lantern Corps teams with Starfleet to thwart some multiversal threat? Could the IMF team from Mission: Impossible recruit members of the Suicide Squad? Freddy Krueger vs. Ghostface? The Conjuring investigators visit a household from Paranormal Activity? Aquaman meets SpongeBob? Krypto pals around with Paw Patrol? What if that mysterious evil from Smile found its way to Gotham City and drew the attention of a certain Clown Prince of Crime? I think you get the idea of where this could go. Crossovers, of course, are nothing new. The Universal Monsters were doing that decades ago. Who Framed Roger Rabbit? famously teamed Looney Tunes and Disney characters. More recently, The LEGO Movie franchise saw Superman, Lando Calrissian and Gandalf all share the screen, while the Ready Player One movie enlisted nearly every major pop culture IP under the sun. The likelihood of Warners-Paramount crossover films happening seems more possible now that so much IP is owned by the same giant media company. Perhaps such intermingling between these IPs will never happen (or not to the scale I’ve suggested here) … or maybe I just foretold a future where crossover slop and $300 million glorified fan fic films are the next big thing. Maybe we’re looking at a cinematic phase of gods and monsters after all, just not the ones we expected.
items.title_en: Skydance Owning Both Warner Bros. and Paramount Could Open the Door to a Future of Crossover Slop

items.title: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Reportedly Had Third Affair With Another Employee
items.excerpt: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned today amid a scandal involving an affair with a suspected Chinese spy and an executive that reported to him. Now, it's been reported that Huang allegedly had an affair with a second employee.
items.content_text: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned today amid a scandal involving an affair with a suspected Chinese spy and an executive that reported to him. Now, it's been reported that Huang allegedly had an affair with a second employee. Huang allegedly had an intimate relationship with a second employee, according to two sources inside Nvidia and reported by Reuters . However, Reuters hasn't named the second employee, and attempts to reach her were not successful. This third revelation comes just hours after Huang resigned from Nvidia, following an internal investigation that kicked off on Sunday . Huang himself came out and admitted to one of the affairs in a letter sent to Nvidia staff and obtained by The BBC . Then, following a meeting where Nvidia's board weighed ousting Huang, the former CEO resigned. In the meantime, Nvidia's board has named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO while the company searches for a new leader. Nvidia is considering both internal and external applicants, but there has been talk that Apple Senior Vice President of Hardware Technlogy Johny Srouji is being considered for the role, according to MacRumors . As for Huang itself, it's not clear where he's going to end up, or what he's going to do going forward. Last night, Elon Musk posted on X that it "would be an honor" to hire Huang ... but it's doubtful that he'd end up at any of Musk's companies. Either way, Huang has been leading Nvidia since 1993, and has seen the company grow from being a niche gaming hardware company to the backbone of the entire AI industry. His resignation is going to send shockwaves throughout the entire tech biz. One of the biggest casualties might end up being PC gaming altogether. After all, Nvidia makes up for a massive 73% of Steam's install base, according to the latest Steam Hardware survey , but the company still dropped gaming from its earnings reports earlier this year. And, now with Jensen's departure, it's unlikely that PC hardware is going to get the same level of support . Photo by Joel Saget / AFP via Getty Images.
items.title_en: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Reportedly Had Third Affair With Another Employee

items.title: Valheim Is Getting a Comic Book Series, and It Looks Badass
items.excerpt: Valheim is expanding beyond video games once again, this time with an official comic book series featuring an impressive lineup of talent from Marvel, DC, television, and animation.
items.content_text: Valheim is expanding beyond video games once again, this time with an official comic book series featuring an impressive lineup of talent from Marvel, DC, television, and animation. Developer Iron Gate Studio has teamed up with GUNGNIR Books and MOOD Publishing to bring its Viking survival game to comics, with the first release planned for the first quarter of 2027. The multi-issue series will feature original stories set in the world of Valheim, rather than simply retelling the events of the game. The writing team certainly has a pretty impressive portfolio that bodes well for the series. It includes Steve Orlando (Wonder Woman, Avengers), Deric A. Hughes and Ben Raab (Quantum Leap), J. Holtham (The Handmaid's Tale, Supergirl), Brea Grant (12 Hour Shift), Tim Sheridan (Masters of the Universe), and Olan Rogers (Final Space). They're joined by TD Orel, Chris Klian, Andrew Sanders, and GUNGNIR Books founder Matthew Medney. On the art side, Scott Oakley, Vanessa Del Rey, Lucas Pereira, and Mario Del Pennino are among the confirmed artists, with Mohamad Samah overseeing production design. More talent is expected to be announced. According to the announcement, the series will explore the mythology of Valheim's mysterious tenth Norse realm, introducing new adventures and perspectives on its gods, monsters, and dangerous environments. Expect plenty of exploration, survival, and presumably some very unfortunate encounters with the local wildlife. This is Valheim, and we're going to make it epic. “Valheim is one of those rare worlds that feels like it existed long before we ever discovered it. There are gods, monsters, entire civilizations, and a mythology so rich that the stories we can tell feel almost endless," said Matthew Medney from GUNGNIR Books. "For us, the opportunity to work alongside Iron Gate and MOOD Publishing to bring this universe into comics is extraordinary. And we've assembled an absolute army of creative talent to do it. We're not interested in simply retelling what millions of players have already experienced. We want to explore the legends that haven't been told, the corners of this world that haven't been seen, and create something that feels worthy of the incredible universe Iron Gate built. This is Valheim, and we're going to make it epic." The comic marks another expansion for Valheim , which has now sold more than 17 million copies worldwide since launching into Steam Early Access in February 2021. The game has already made the jump to tabletop gaming with Valheim: The Board Game, also developed in partnership with MOOD Publishing. For now, there's no specific release date beyond Q1 2027, and details about individual issues, collectible editions, and how fans can get involved are still to come. In the meantime, Valheim players can look forward to exploring the tenth realm without having to worry about keeping their food buffs topped up. Which, frankly, sounds rather nice.

items.title: Fable Drops Four Minutes of New Gameplay
items.excerpt: Four minutes of new Fable gameplay has been released by Xbox, showing off more of the game's combat.
items.content_text: Four minutes of new Fable gameplay has been released by Xbox, showing off more of the game's combat. The footage was released personally by Xbox CEO Asha Sharma as part of a larger celebration for the company's 25th anniversary. The gameplay shows off a bunch of combat, highlighting not only standard swordplay, but also ranged attacks and unique moves that can be performed using magic. The gameplay was captured on PC using ultra graphics settings and concludes with the protagonist stumbling upon an incredibly sinister-looking tomb or coffin. Fable was, of course, meant to have been released this fall . However, Xbox made the smart decision to delay the game to February . Although the team says the delay wasn't done specifically in an effort to avoid GTA 6 , it was likely a nice benefit. Microsoft still had plenty of releases this autumn thanks to Modern Warfare 4 and Gears of War: E-Day, so it was wise to give Fable some more room to breathe. The game was announced all the way back in 2020, but has been in some form of development at Playground Games for nearly a decade. Forza Horizon studio Playground Games is leading the charge on the title, though it has recruited a bunch of talent from around the industry so that it is well-equipped to build an RPG. Fable is one of the most anticipated games on Xbox's slate, partially because it's one of the most beloved RPG franchises out there, and Microsoft is looking for a big win in the AAA space outside of shooters. Fable is also coming to PS5, as it had been previously announced for the platform. It'll be interesting to see what happens if the game performs well on the platform. Xbox is trying to lean more into exclusivity, but it unfortunately didn't seem to pay off for Gears of War: E-Day . Here's hoping Fable is worth the wait and pays off on Microsoft's investments. Fable will release on Xbox Series X|S, PS5, and PC on February 23.

items.title: ‘Maybe We’ve Gone a Step Too Far’ — Ocarina of Time Remake Producer Reveals the Game's ReDeads Were Originally Supposed to Be Even Scarier
items.excerpt: Producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi explained why the development team behind the Ocarina of Time Remake toned down the ReDeads to make them less scary.
items.content_text: Producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi explained why the development team behind the Ocarina of Time Remake toned down the ReDeads to make them less scary. If you grew up playing the original Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo 64, you were probably traumatized by some of the game’s famously frightening enemies like the Gibdos, ReDeads, and Dead Hands. These last two were particularly terrifying for young players at the time — partially because we were still kids, and partially due to the N64’s graphical limitations that forced our minds to fill in the visual gaps in the monsters’ designs. These enemies were a particular talking point when the Remake was first announced. Some players were doubtful that this new game could truly capture the terror of the original monsters, since a) it’s a game that’s also supposed to appeal to children and b) the updated graphics of modern Nintendo consoles don’t necessarily allow for the ‘fear of the unknown’ phenomena afforded to low-fidelity titles like 1999's Silent Hill . (There’s an entire genre of indie horror games that pursue this aesthetic for a reason, after all.) Speaking with Gamespot , producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi explained that the Remake’s updated graphics actually made the ReDeads extremely scary at first. And while the development team was supposedly enthusiastic about this aspect of the project, he and fellow producer Eiji Aonuma felt that this detail wasn’t necessarily true to the original experience of the first game. "With this remake, the graphics are a lot improved, and so the ReDead – the sound, the graphics, and the movement – ended up being very, very scary,” Fujibayashi said. “And the staff wanted to make this in service of making a good gameplay experience. But from our perspective, taking a step back, we felt like, ‘Let's remember the experience that we don't want to change, and taking that into consideration, maybe we've gone a step too far, so let's dial it back.’" That being said, plenty of players feel that the Remake’s ReDeads are still sufficiently terrifying. items.title: Doom Developer id Software Confirms Work on New Game, Will Be Directed by Hugo Martin
items.excerpt: At Xbox's 25th anniversary celebration at its Fan Fest event in Seattle, id Software confirmed that it is working on a new game, wrapping up last year's Doom: The Dark Ages with the release of the upcoming Slaughter Mode on November 16.
items.content_text: At Xbox's 25th anniversary celebration at its Fan Fest event in Seattle, id Software confirmed that it is working on a new game, wrapping up last year's Doom: The Dark Ages with the release of the upcoming Slaughter Mode on November 16. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma made the announcement on her X account, posting , "Few studios have shaped the first-person shooter genre as much as id Software. Slaughter Mode comes to DOOM: The Dark Ages | Revelations on November 16, and the team is already working on its next game." id itself also posted , saying, "We're incredibly excited about our next project, a new game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin. It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on." Whether that next project is more Doom, or perhaps id returning to its other big franchise, Quake, remains to be seen. Or it might be neither of those and could be something new entirely. Although it's worth noting that id Software is under Xbox's Bethesda arm, and Bethesda boss Jill Braff recently told its development teams that "we are shifting from a planning model primarily centered on what's next for each independent studio to one that focuses on our strongest franchises and determining the content roadmap that best serves our players and Bethesda as a whole." So perhaps Quake or a fourth Doom game are the more likely options? That remains to be seen, but what the last decade has proven is that Martin and the id Software team are very good at what they do. Doom (2016) successfully rebooted a dormant franchise, while Doom Eternal stood on its shoulders , and then Doom: The Dark Ages brought the focus back to the ground . All three were excellent. Doom: The Dark Ages' Slaughter Mode, meanwhile, is an endless single-player mode that will be added as a free update for those who've purchased Doom: The Dark Ages - Revelations DLC, which we reviewed and loved .

items.title: As Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns, the Future of GeForce Hangs in the Balance
items.excerpt: After 33 years, Jensen Huang has resigned from Nvidia, following a scandal involving a suspected Chinese spy. And while this has all kinds of implications for the economy as a whole, in our own little world of PC gaming, it's looking increasingly unlikely that GeForce is going to get much attention going forward, now that CFO Colette Kress has stepped up as interim CEO.
items.content_text: After 33 years, Jensen Huang has resigned from Nvidia , following a scandal involving a suspected Chinese spy. This has all kinds of implications for the economy as a whole but Huang's exit will certainly have a ripple effect on the world of PC gaming, too. With Nvidia CFO Collette Kress stepping in as interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent replacement, it's looking increasingly unlikely that GeForce is going to get much attention going forward. Kress joined Nvidia in 2013, as the GeForce GTX 780 was coming out , and has helped guide the company through its transformation into a data center and AI powerhouse. Before Nvidia, she was at Cisco as the CFO of Business Technology and Operations Finance, and before that, she was CFO of the Servers and Tools Group at Microsoft. Her history, combined with Nvidia's current trajectory, means that AI is still going to be Nvidia's main business. After all, Nvidia has made hundreds of billions of dollars pursuing AI, so having a CFO in charge, even in the interim, probably means Team Green is going to push even harder for the AI market. On the surface, then, nothing would really be changing for the company. I've been covering Nvidia for more than a decade now, and I've watched in real time as GeForce has become a smaller and smaller part of its CES showcases. Just this year, Nvidia straight up dropped gaming from its earnings reports , combining the category with "edge computing," along with robotics and mobile computing. Nvidia almost certainly would have continued deprioritizing GeForce, regardless of Huang's exit. The difference, though, is that Huang has been with Nvidia from the beginning, when it was primarily a gaming company. Despite pushing AI as the centerpiece of Nvidia's mission since at least 2016, he at least recognized that gaming was great for Nvidia's public image and would throw gamers a bone every now and then. To be clear, I don't think Nvidia is going to be exiting the gaming business any time soon. Nvidia has a stranglehold on the entire PC gaming market, and it'd be bad business to walk away from a space where they have a near monopoly. There will still probably be new GeForce cards coming out — it's likely the RTX 60 series will come out in 2028 — but I think there's a real risk of Nvidia growing complacent with its market share and releasing worse products as the company invests most of its R&D into its data center business. There had already been signs of things getting worse for PC gamers. The RTX 50 series had a couple of duds and had brutal price hikes across the board. But no matter how you look at it, Nvidia's current-generation graphics cards are still the best in the business and are supported by a wide swath of software that is unmatched by AMD and Intel. I would love to be proven wrong, but I could see GeForce falling into a slump parallel to Intel's after Skylake in 2015, when Team Blue followed its consumer CPUs with more and more rebadges of the same architecture (Kaby Lake, Coffee Lake, etc.) because it had consumer market dominance and simply made more money elsewhere. During that time, Intel also had a transitional CEO, Brian Krzanich, who helped Intel expand into other industries. AMD could get its act together and come out with something awesome to compete, just like it did with Ryzen in 2017. But AMD CEO Lisa Su has said in a recent interview with Yahoo Finance that "we are a data-center first company," so the odds of that happening are looking grim. The real casualties from the fallout are probably going to be the weirder gaming releases that Nvidia sprinkles throughout the year. In January, that was G-Sync Pulsar , a new form of G-Sync, which flickers the backlight of your gaming monitor to trick your eyes into thinking the display is running at a higher refresh rate. That technology was essentially a passion project that had been cooking in the background for years before finally landing in a few gaming monitors at CES 2026. Tto this day I wish it was found in more gaming monitors . I suspect GeForce is going to look a lot different than it does now in a few years. If Nvidia ends up with a CEO who has a career history anything like Kress's, I'd expect less of a focus on GPUs you can slot into your gaming PC, and more of a focus on funneling more GPUs into data centers. I just hope that I'm wrong.

items.title: AI Usage Up, PS6 and Xbox Helix Development Still Low in Newest GDC Dev Survey
items.excerpt: GDC Festival of Gaming organizers released the data from their 15th annual game developer survey, the State of the Game Industry report. Over 2600 game developers anonymously responded, and the results show increased generative AI usage, not too many developers working on PlayStation 6 or Xbox Project Helix next-gen projects as of yet, an increase in the number of developers in a union, and more.
items.content_text: GDC Festival of Gaming organizers released the data from their 15th annual game developer survey, the State of the Game Industry report. Over 2,600 game developers anonymously responded, and the results show increased generative AI usage, not too many developers working on PlayStation 6 or Xbox Project Helix next-gen projects as of yet, an increase in the number of developers in a union, and more. "40% of game industry professionals report using generative AI tools as part of their job, up four points from the previous survey," GDC reported. "57% of AI adopters use it daily. Usage is highest among those working at mobile-only studios (70%) and those working on free-to-play games (58%). Company policy tends to vary significantly by company size, with 27% of AAA workers feeling encouraged or pressured to use generative AI, compared to only 9% of indie studio workers." However, the report continued, "despite the industry’s increased adoption of generative AI, its use remains polarizing; 55% of respondents felt that it has a negative impact on games, which is consistent with 54% from the previous survey. Responses suggest that game industry professionals are forming nuanced stances on the topic. For instance, some respondents wrote that they see value in using generative AI tools for repetitive tasks, research, and prototyping, but others cited environmental, psychological, and societal concerns for their hesitation to use such tools. Others pondered whether generative AI could be an equalizer for marginalized and excluded groups struggling with cost, geography, or access." Meanwhile, 10% of survey respondents are currently developing for PS6, with 8% currently working on Xbox's Project Helix. VR, augumented reality, or mixed reality game development is down to 3% of people surveyed, while Switch 2 development interest is up almost 10% to 47% this year. Interestingly, overall support in the US for game industry worker unionization was down a tad, from 82% to 80%, but more respondents reported being part of a union – 15% this year compared to 12% last year. Finally and unfortunately, a whopping 65% of those responding to the survey said that their mental health has suffered because of their job and the long hours – and that's for those who are still employed. A full third of respondents have been laid off in the last two years, with two-thirds of that group saying they were laid off in the past year. And sadly, more than half (54%) of those who've been laid off have yet to find another job, though not for a lack of trying: 62% say they've applied for 20 or more jobs, with over a quarter (27%) saying they've applied for over a hundred . Overall, one-fifth of survey respondents (21%) are unemployed, up from 13% in the last report. The next Game Developers Conference: Festival of Gaming will take place in San Francisco on March 1–4, 2027.

items.title: The Game Awards 2026 are Coming to Disney+

items.content_text: This year’s Game Awards are coming to Disney+, where it will broadcast in addition to its usual streams on Twitch and YouTube. This partnership with Disney comes as the media monolith seeks to promote its roster of video games and game-related media projects, which Kingdom Hearts fans will note comes right on the heels of its big KH4 reveal at D23 earlier this year. Reports from Variety state that this packed slate includes Disney Twisted-Wonderland: The Animation, as well as Death Stranding Isolations , the forthcoming anime series based on Hideo Kojima’s Death Stranding franchise. The show got its first proper trailer in late October, alongside a first look at a full-length anime film set in the Death Stranding universe, Mosquito , which is set for a theatrical release on an as-yet unannounced date. Resident Evil 9, 007: First Light, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake are just a few of the heavy hitters in an already packed slate — not to mention GTA 6, which will qualify for the Awards by the skin of its teeth after its arrival on November 19. items.title: Doctor Doom Is Not a Tony Stark Variant in Avengers: Doomsday, Confirms Kevin Feige
items.excerpt: Kevin Feige has confirmed that Doctor Doom is not a variant of Tony Stark in Avengers: Doomsday.
items.content_text: Kevin Feige has confirmed that Doctor Doom is not a variant of Tony Stark in Avengers: Doomsday . When speaking with Empire Magazine, Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige debunked the popular fan theory that Doctor Doom and Tony Stark have a shared connection in the multiverse. Fans have speculated that Doom is a "variant" of Stark, since Robert Downey Jr. plays both characters . Variants are other versions of a character across the multiverse. We've seen this with the three Spider-Men, Wolverine, and Loki, so naturally, some fans thought this may all be an elaborate way to explain how Robert Downey Jr. is also playing Doom... turns out, it's not. “Is Steve Rogers a Johnny Storm variant?" asked Feige. "People wondered, ‘Is Doom just a variant of another character? Is this just a shortcut to bringing back another character?’ The answer is no. He’s Victor Von Doom.” As for what Doom's whole deal is, the creative team behind the film teased what kind of energy he brings and why he is the way he is. The Russo Brothers, who are directing the film, teased that Doom has lost a child, is a "victim of trauma" and has a greater ego than Thanos. They also noted that he's a pretty terrifying presence. "Doom is a Gothic character,” said director Joe Russo. “He says, ‘Hell answers to me,’ and he’s not kidding. He’s a very powerful character with some very dark magic, and he’s not above selling his soul to get what he wants. He’s worth being scared of.” Robert Downey Jr. also noted that he was excited to lean into being a villain this time around, and suggested that Doom's plans have a tremendous scope to them. "I like a bit of scorched earth,” teases Downey Jr. “Whatever you think he may be entertaining, I would ten times it, and you’ll probably be closer to the ballpark." There's still a lot that we don't know about the film, which is just a little over a month away from being released. A recent listing on the WGA's website credited Hugh Jackman and Ryan Reynolds for contributing to the film's script, which seems to suggest Wolverine and Deadpool may be in the film . Additionally, Marvel confirmed earlier this week that Scarlet Witch will also return in Avengers: Doomsday , though seemingly under the control of Doom himself. Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on December 18.

items.title: The Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power Season 3 Resolves One of the Most Fascinating Mysteries From Middle-earth Lore
items.excerpt: Rings of Power Season 3 has revealed the true identity of Ciarán Hinds’ Dark Wizard, thereby resolving one of the biggest mysteries from J.R.R. Tolkien's Middle-earth lore.
items.content_text: Full spoilers ahead for the first four episodes of The Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power Season 3! Prime Video has released the first four episodes of The Rings of Power Season 3, and they’re nothing if not eventful. But amid all the warring and hoarding of magical rings, there’s also a reveal that has a lot of Tolkien nerds’ heads spinning. The series has resolved what may well be the biggest lingering mystery from Tolkien’s vast Middle-earth mythology. Read on for a full breakdown of the big reveal in Episode 3 and how it resolves a major loose end from books like The Silmarillion and Unfinished Tales of Middle-earth. Ciarán Hinds’ Dark Wizard Revealed Back in Season 2, viewers were introduced to a new antagonist played by Ciarán Hinds. Known as the “Dark Wizard,” this villain reigns over the cursed land of Rhûn. Gandalf (Daniel Weyman) is desperate to put a stop to this powerful foe, lest the Dark Wizard ally himself with Sauron and create a truly unstoppable army. Though Rings of Power is set many centuries before the events of The Lord of the Rings trilogy, many of the characters are designed to evoke familiar archetypes from the movies. Once again, we have a saga crammed full of noble elves, intrepid dwarves, plucky Hobbits (or Harfoots), and morally conflicted men. But sometimes those archetypes are subverted in the end. Much like how the seemingly Aragorn-esque Halbrand (Charlie Vickers) turned out to be Sauron, the Dark Wizard isn’t who many fans assumed him to be. More From Middle-earth The Rings of Power Season 3, Episodes 1-4 Review and Recap This Is Where the Rings Are in Rings of Power Season 3 The Rings of Power Stars React to This Week's Big Season 3 Deaths Initially, Hinds’ character was speculated to be Saruman, given that he’s a dark wizard with great ambitions and a willingness to fight alongside Sauron. But that never quite made sense, as it’s not until the end of the Third Age that Saruman allows his true motivations to be known. Season 3, Episode 3 instead confirms a different fan theory, revealing the Dark Wizard to be a being known as Pallando. Tolkien didn’t write a great deal about Pallando (we’ll get more into that shortly), but the gist is that Eru Ilúvatar (the God of this fantasy universe) originally sent five wizards to Middle-earth to aid the kingdoms of elves and men in their war against Sauron. Alongside Gandalf the Grey, there were also Saruman the White, Radagast the Brown, and the two Blue Wizards, Alatar and Pallando. Radagast became mostly distracted by his love of the wilderness and animals, and the two Blue Wizards vanished into obscurity, leaving only Gandalf and Saruman to carry on the fight into the Third Age. The series extrapolates on this backstory by revealing Hinds to be Pallando. In a conversation with the disembodied form of Eru Ilúvatar, Gandalf learns that Pallando became corrupted by his thirst for power and murdered Alatar. That act poisoned the realm of Rhûn. Despite this, Gandalf’s mission isn’t to stop Pallando, but to appeal to his better nature and convince him to stop his army from joining Sauron. Even Dark Wizards can be redeemed, it seems. What Did Tolkien Reveal About the Blue Wizards? The two Blue Wizards were never a big focus of Tolkien’s writings, which perhaps explains why they’re a source of such fascination among fans. They don’t appear at all in The Hobbit or The Lord of the Rings trilogy, leaving only a handful of scattered references in posthumously published works like Unfinished Tales of Middle-earth and The Peoples of Middle-earth. As Tolkien established, Pallando was one of five Maiar (immortal beings of the same race as Sauron himself) who were handpicked to travel from the Undying Lands to Middle-earth to help rally resistance against Sauron. Pallando and Alatar were known as the Blue Wizards (or “Ithryn Luin” in the ancient language of Sindarin) because of their distinctive sea blue robes. Originally, only Alatar, Gandalf, and Saruman were chosen for this quest, but Alatar opted to invite Pallando along, and Radagast was also added to the group for some reason. Once in Middle-earth, the various wizards split up and picked different areas to focus on. Saruman, Alatar, and Pallando journeyed east to appeal to the Easterlings and the Haradrim. And that’s about where the latter two characters’ story ends in Tolkien’s writings. Saruman eventually returned to the West and set up shop in Isengard, but Alatar and Pallando never came with him. They just disappeared, hence why when Ian McKellen’s Gandalf mentions the Blue Wizards in 2012’s The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey, he can’t even remember their names (technically, that was because the filmmakers didn’t have the rights to use characters from Unfinished Tales). Tolkien himself seemed pretty pessimistic about whether the Blue Wizards ultimately succeeded in their mission. Tolkien himself seemed pretty pessimistic about whether the Blue Wizards ultimately succeeded in their mission. In a letter published after his death, Tolkien wrote, “I think that they went as emissaries to distant regions, east and south... Missionaries to enemy-occupied lands as it were. What success they had I do not know; but I fear that they failed, as Saruman did, though doubtless in different ways; and I suspect they were founders or beginners of secret cults and ‘magic’ traditions that outlasted the fall of Sauron." This lack of textual information has only fueled speculation about the Blue Wizards over the decades, to the point where they’ve become a major source of fascination for hardcore Tolkien nerds. What actually became of Alatar and Pallando? Now we finally know. Obviously, Rings of Power is doing a lot of embellishing to build on what little Tolkien established about these characters. Now we know that Alatar and Pallando didn’t just fail in their mission; the latter actively became the sort of threat he was designed to quash. However, the series is hinting that there may still be a redemption arc in store for Pallando. The character is currently subservient to Sauron, but we suspect that’ll change as the final seasons of the show unfold. There may still be a chance for this fallen wizard to do some good and play a part in Sauron’s downfall, even if he’s doomed to be forgotten by history. For more on Rings of Power, check out IGN’s review of Season 3, Episodes 1-4 and learn more about the big character deaths in these episodes . Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN.
